name: Combining Financial and Non-Financial Data
title: Combining Financial and Non-Financial Data
answer: Combining financial and non-financial data means bringing together traditional accounting figures, such as revenue, capital expenditure, and operating costs, with sustainability metrics like greenhouse gas emissions, water use, and workforce demographics. In carbon accounting this often involves pairing spend data from procurement or general ledger systems with activity data such as kilowatt hours, litres of fuel, or tonnes of purchased materials. The goal is to produce a single view of performance where a company can see both the cost and the carbon impact of a business decision. This work sits inside the broader field of sustainability reporting and management accounting, not financial audit itself.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Combining financial and non-financial data means bringing together traditional accounting figures, such as revenue, capital expenditure, and operating costs, with sustainability metrics like greenhouse gas emissions, water use, and workforce demographics. In carbon accounting this often involves pairing spend data from procurement or general ledger systems with activity data such as kilowatt hours, litres of fuel, or tonnes of purchased materials. The goal is to produce a single view of performance where a company can see both the cost and the carbon impact of a business decision. This work sits inside the broader field of sustainability reporting and management accounting, not financial audit itself.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work typically runs on existing enterprise systems rather than specialised AI hardware. Financial data comes from ERP platforms and spreadsheets, while non-financial data may live in utility invoices, supplier surveys, sensor feeds, or dedicated ESG reporting software. A common pattern is a cloud data warehouse or lake where both data types are landed, cleaned, and joined using shared keys such as cost centre, supplier, or purchase order. Compute needs are modest, usually batch processing on standard servers or managed cloud services, with occasional use of document parsing tools for invoices and reports.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: The core method is data integration and allocation rather than predictive modelling. Practitioners map financial line items to emission factors or other sustainability indicators, often following standards like the Greenhouse Gas Protocol. Machine learning is used mainly for extracting data from unstructured documents, matching supplier names across systems, and estimating missing activity data where direct measurement is unavailable. The output is usually a set of reconciled tables or dashboards that show, for example, emissions per dollar of revenue or per unit produced. Quality control relies on reconciliation checks between financial totals and non-financial totals.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Combining these data types raises questions about data ownership, accuracy, and auditability. Financial figures are subject to internal controls and external audit, while non-financial data often has weaker provenance and less consistent definitions. A professional should document the source, transformation, and allocation rules for every non-financial metric, and keep a clear trail from raw activity data to reported figures. Rights and risk centre on supplier confidentiality, because detailed activity data can reveal commercially sensitive information, and on the risk of double counting or misallocation across business units. No single regulator currently sets a universal standard for this combined data, so practice varies by jurisdiction and reporting framework.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: The direction is toward more automated, continuous integration of financial and non-financial data, driven by expanding disclosure requirements and investor demand. Expect tighter links between procurement systems and carbon accounting, so that a purchase order carries both a price and an estimated emissions factor at the point of approval. As standards converge, the distinction between financial and non-financial data may blur into a single general ledger for all material resources. The main constraint will remain data quality and the cost of collecting primary activity data, not the capability of the software.
